meta.title: StreamSuites programme roadmap
meta.note: Conservative programme estimates based on the current workspace. Percentages are directional, not mathematically exact completion measurements.

initiatives.title: Runtime, Auth & shared state
initiatives.description: The central Runtime/Auth authority already owns accounts, sessions, permissions, rooms, destinations, alerts, exports, audit state, and canonical version projections. Current work continues to harden these contracts and close integration gaps without moving authority into client repositories.
initiatives.next_milestone: Broaden end-to-end authority and recovery validation across connected clients.

initiatives.title: Public, Creator, Admin & Developer surfaces
initiatives.description: The public site, Creator, Admin, and Developer clients now expose a substantial set of account, content, diagnostics, version, and operational views. They remain clients of Runtime/Auth, with several workflows and developer capabilities still intentionally partial or placeholder-backed.
initiatives.next_milestone: Finish authoritative wiring for the remaining partial client workflows.

initiatives.title: Browser Studio
initiatives.description: Browser Studio has private-room foundations, Cloudflare Realtime collaboration, layout and branding work, and creator-facing room tooling. Broadcast output, recording, and broader provider workflows are not presented as production-ready and the product remains off air.
initiatives.next_milestone: Turn the proven room and collaboration foundation into a validated broadcast path.

initiatives.title: Native StudioApp & media engine
initiatives.description: The Windows-native WPF and C++ application has real local capture, preview, composition, audio, recording, replay, output, scene, and engine-supervision foundations. Remote media, provider output, filters, virtual camera, and broader physical-device acceptance remain open work.
initiatives.next_milestone: Close real-media continuity and device acceptance gaps across supported source paths.

initiatives.title: Studio for OBS
initiatives.description: The OBS integration has a hardened multi-slot RealtimeKit receiver foundation and preserves OBS ownership of capture, mixing, encoding, recording, and output. Production chat, alerts, automation, native decode, and automatic layout remain outside the shipped integration depth.
initiatives.next_milestone: Validate supported OBS packaging and expand the safe receiver-to-workflow bridge.

initiatives.title: Platform integrations & destinations
initiatives.description: Runtime/Auth includes destination and integration authority with working foundations across the product family, but provider depth is uneven and not every surfaced destination represents a complete production workflow. Credentials remain backend-owned and secret-safe.
initiatives.next_milestone: Complete and verify destination flows one provider contract at a time.

initiatives.title: Live chat, automation, alerts & creator tools
initiatives.description: The workspace contains creator-scoped chat, alert, automation, audience, export, and public-tool foundations, with runtime ownership and permission boundaries established. Product coverage and live provider behavior are still being expanded and validated.
initiatives.next_milestone: Connect more creator workflows to authoritative, observable runtime events.

initiatives.title: Release engineering, packaging & documentation
initiatives.description: Canonical version exports, protected download surfaces, native packaging work, release notes, and a dedicated documentation site are in place. Independent product release states, clean-machine acceptance, licensing gates, and deployment evidence continue to limit broad release-readiness claims.
initiatives.next_milestone: Strengthen repeatable packaging, compatibility, and published-release evidence.
